title: Conflict Analysis and Restarts in Mixed Integer Programming
abstract:
Mixed Integer Programming and Constraint Programming can be viewed as
two flavors of the same fundamental paradigm: solving discrete
optimization problems by traversing a search tree with partial
variable assignments and backtracking. From a high level, the
differences are more in the details: while Constraint Programming is
mostly about finding feasible solutions using efficient
special-purpose domain propagation algorithms, mixed integer
programming is more driven by the objective function and puts the LP
relaxation into its algorithmic core.

While CP and MIP started independently in two different research
communities, they inspired each other over the years, and techniques
from one were adopted by the other.

Two such techniques that originated in the SAT and CP world are
conflict analysis and restarts. Nowadays, these two, together with
domain propagation, are the central components of state-of-the-art SAT
and CP solvers. They have been adopted by MIP solvers as well. While
not being as fundamental as in SAT and CP, they still provide a major
performance improvement for MIP solvers.

In this talk, we shed some light on how conflict analysis and restarts
are being used inside the Gurobi MIP solver and why their role in MIP
is a little different from their SAT and CP counterparts.
keywords: Mixed Integer Programming, Conflict Analysis, Restarts
